mechanism.name: Lin et al. (2024) linear IV adapted from pinned WIT code

generation_equations.label: Instrument distribution
generation_equations.expression: Z_i ~ N_21(0, Sigma_Z); (Sigma_Z)_{jk} = 0.8 * 0.3^{|j-k|} for j,k=1,...,21, including diagonal entries 0.8.

generation_equations.label: Joint structural error distribution
generation_equations.expression: (epsilon_i, eta_i)^T ~ N_2(0, [[1, 0.6], [0.6, 1]]); both variances are 1 and Corr(epsilon_i,eta_i)=0.6, following the pinned author code.

generation_equations.label: Sampling independence
generation_equations.expression: Z_i is independent of (epsilon_i, eta_i). The vectors (Z_i, epsilon_i, eta_i) are iid across individuals i=1,...,n; epsilon_i and eta_i are correlated within an individual.

generation_equations.label: Common fixed parameters
generation_equations.expression: p=21; beta=1; alpha=(0 repeated 9 times, 0.4 repeated 6 times, 0.2 repeated 6 times)^T. Thus Z1-Z9 have zero direct outcome coefficients, while Z10-Z21 have nonzero direct coefficients.

generation_equations.label: Default code_case_2 first-stage coefficients
generation_equations.expression: In code_case_2 (default), gamma=0.15*1_21. This is the active Case 2 setting of the pinned author script.

generation_equations.label: Alternative code_case_1 first-stage coefficients
generation_equations.expression: In code_case_1, gamma=0.4*1_21. This enables the commented Case 1 setting; it is another scenario of the same mechanism family.

generation_equations.label: Continuous outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y_i = beta*D_i + Z_i^T alpha + epsilon_i. Only Z1,...,Z21,D,Y are observed outputs; epsilon and eta are internal disturbances.

sampling.dependence: iid individuals; correlated Z components and correlated epsilon/eta within individuals; Z independent of errors

assumptions: Z independent of structural errors; positive definite covariances; nonzero first stage
Z1-Z9 have zero direct effects conditional on other instruments; Z10-Z21 violate exclusion

When validity is unknown, identification requires a rule such as plurality of equal reduced-form/first-stage coefficient ratios: valid group size 9 exceeds either invalid group size 6. No majority claimed.
No LATE monotonicity condition for this homogeneous continuous-treatment target

properties.notes: No baseline covariates. 21 candidate instruments, all active in D; 12 direct Y effects. Instrument count recorded separately from baseline dimension. Fixed p=21, source n=500/1000, smoke n=128. Linear Gaussian SEM.

estimand.name: beta
estimand.definition: Homogeneous structural coefficient: E[Y(do(D=d+1))-Y(do(D=d))]=beta for the specified superpopulation; both scenarios beta=1. Not LATE.

truth.expression: Homogeneous structural coefficient: E[Y(do(D=d+1))-Y(do(D=d))]=beta for the specified superpopulation; both scenarios beta=1. Not LATE.
truth.derivation: Analytic intervention contrast beta, population reduced-form coefficients and independent moment diagnostics.

adaptations: Use pinned author code covariance Sigma_Z[j,k]=0.8*0.3^abs(j-k); publication covariance typesetting unresolved.
Use code error variances 1 and 1, correlation 0.6; publication text specifies epsilon SD 0.5 and eta SD 1.
Default code_case_2 gamma=0.15; code_case_1 enables commented gamma=0.4. README says Case 1 while active script is Case 2.
Independently implement the probability law with NumPy local PCG64/Cholesky; no R/MASS seed-level equivalence claimed.
Accept n and seed; omit estimator comparisons, 500 repetitions and overwritten concentration calculations.
